name: Lava Lamp
description: Sol, a study in slow matter. Warm wax rises, cools and falls, joining and separating inside a softly lit glass vessel.

assets.credit: Original Sol wax field, glass vessel and material rendering

compatibility: WebGL2 for the analytic density field; a lower-resolution Canvas 2D fallback uses the same density function. Canvas 2D composes the glass and base. No external runtime dependencies or assets.
ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, native dialog and CSS container queries. Keyboard and touch operate the ordinary HTML controls. Reduced motion starts paused; Resume is explicit.
Hidden or offscreen lamps suspend rendering and simulation. Context restoration recreates the shader resources. Disposal releases observers, animation frames, WebGL programs, buffers and context.
notes: Sol is original procedural artwork: a thermal parcel model with a smooth Gaussian density surface, analytic normal lighting, a translucent glass chamber, metal or ceramic pedestal and soft environmental illumination.

Wax heats at the bottom and cools at the top, retaining thermal memory between those regions. Buoyancy, viscosity, pair cohesion, thermal shear and a weak convection current evolve the parcels at a fixed 120 Hz simulation step.

Surface merging and splitting are genuine changes in the connected implicit field. The mass-carrying parcels remain in the model, while their overlapping fields form necks, pools and separate droplets. They are not individually painted circles.
This is a physically informed two-dimensional simulation with depth lighting, not a full three-dimensional fluid solver. The controls change forces, shape, surface threshold or optical rendering.

Classic, giant ambient and minimal column views share the same engine. Six presets, five palettes, fullscreen inspection, pause, thirty-second advance, PNG output and shared settings/source export are included.
reuse: WaxField in model.js has no DOM dependencies. It exposes advance, reset, update, parcels and snapshot; sampleField gives matching density and analytic gradients for custom rendering.

createWaxRenderer renders only the fluid field. createLampRenderer adds a separate shell. createLavaLamp owns canvas sizing, lifecycle and playback; other websites can use any of these layers independently.
The portable source ZIP includes a complete studio and a neutral embed-demo.html with object, column and background placements. No Tampa page logic or third-party imagery is needed.
